extraction.summary: Mr. Bergstrom, a 74-year-old male with CKD, AF, and prostate cancer, was admitted with urosepsis and acute confusion. He was treated with IV co-amoxiclav for a confirmed E. coli UTI and recovered fully with resolution of confusion and improvement in renal function. He is discharged on oral antibiotics and a reduced dose of furosemide. Follow-up is arranged with primary care and renal services.
extraction.clinical_reasoning: The patient's acute presentation was driven by sepsis and acute kidney injury, both of which have shown clinical and laboratory improvement. The creatinine level of 142 umol/L, while technically 'high' relative to the reference range, is an improvement from the patient's baseline of 168 umol/L, supporting the resolution of the AKI. Continued monitoring of renal function and diuretic titration is warranted given his underlying CKD.
recommended_next_steps: GP review of furosemide dose in 2 weeks.
Renal clinic follow-up in 6 weeks with repeat U&E tests.
